verdict.rationale: Paperspace documents Notebooks as a web-based Jupyter IDE on accelerated compute, plus a thin mention of connecting alternative IDEs to remote Jupyter kernels. Machines are reachable over SSH from the console or desktop app, though one hands-on report says SSH access on Core servers was an uphill battle. Nothing documents one-step Jupyter launch on a Machine or a named VS Code/Cursor remote integration. Missing for 10: documented one-click Jupyter or IDE launch on a machine instance, an explicit VS Code/Cursor remote-connect workflow, and independent corroboration that IDE connection works smoothly.

support.subject: As a developer, I can open Jupyter or connect my IDE (VS Code/Cursor) to the instance in one step

citations.quote: Notebooks are a web-based Jupyter IDE with shared persistent storage for long-term development and inter-notebook collaboration, backed by accelerated compute.
Connect to remote Jupyter kernels through alternative IDEs.
You can connect to your Linux or Windows-based machine using the Paperspace console or desktop app using SSH connection.
